parsed.title: Stray '|---|' appended to table rows
parsed.detail: Multiple new ES rows end with a literal '|---|' inside the last cell (e.g. 0.10.0 row: '...publicar el re-empaquetado. |---|'; same on workflow-status 3.5.0, review-change 3.5.1, fold-findings 1.5.0, triage-issue 2.8.0, plan-feature 5.2.0, plan-fix 3.2.0). This adds a spurious extra column to each row, corrupting the markdown tables. The EN rows for the same entries do not carry it.

parsed.title: Header separator reduced to 3 columns while rows have 4+
parsed.detail: The diff changes each ES table header from '|---|---|---|---|' (4 cols) to '|---|---|---|' (3 cols), but the rows (existing and new) still have 4 cells (plus the stray '|---|'), so the separator no longer matches the row shape in the package, workflow-status, review-change, fold-findings, triage-issue, plan-feature and plan-fix tables.

parsed.title: Behavior change shipped as a patch bump
parsed.detail: review-change 3.5.1 is typed 'patch', but the entry describes a routing behavior change: 'the REVIEW-FAIL → Next: block and the Routing table route a replan-in-unit / plan-owned finding through node scripts/unit-route.mjs <unit> ... replacing the two contradictory sentences that sent the class to the executor and to plan-feature separately.' The file's own versioning policy says patch = 'wording, examples, clarifications, internal tidy-ups; no behavior change.' A changed routing destination is a new routing case, which the policy assigns to minor.

parsed.title: Undefined bump type '—' for replan-findings 1.0.0
parsed.detail: The new-skill row uses Type '—', but the declared policy table only defines major/minor/patch bumps; no category or meaning for '—' is declared anywhere in this material, leaving the versioning vocabulary contradicted by its own table.

parsed.title: ES mirror omits review-implementation/replan-findings type mismatch context
parsed.detail: ES row for replan-findings 1.0.0 also uses '—' as type while ES policy table only defines mayor/menor/parche — same undefined-vocabulary issue as the EN side, so the two language versions agree but both contradict the declared policy.
